P001.title: James Spence Sr — Orkney fur trader
P001.text: Born c1753 in Birsay, Orkney. Came to York Factory in 1773 as an HBC labourer and inland voyageur ('a fine fellow and a good canoe man'). Left in charge of Buckingham House in 1793, the HBC's most westerly post at the time. Died there aged 42 in 1795, leaving Margaret pregnant with their fourth child [Verify vs primary records.]

P002.title: Margaret 'Nestichio' Batt — the Métis matriarch
P002.text: Born 1757, daughter of Isaac Batt (c1725-1791), an English HBC inland trader, and an unnamed Cree woman — the matrilineal Métis root of this line. She grew up in the fur-trade world of York Factory, where the young Orkney voyageur James Spence began courting her when she was 16. Family oral tradition (preserved in several written versions since the 1800s) tells that as a girl she was kidnapped by the Blackfeet and her mother asked James to rescue her; after many failed attempts he succeeded using a relay of horses, then waited until she was older to marry her. Over the years they had four children: James, Andrew, George, and Margaret 'Peggy' (your direct ancestor, born 1795/96 just after James Sr died at Buckingham House). Widowed at 38 and pregnant, she raised the four children, returning to York Factory then the Red River Settlement. In 1821 all her children married at Red River — including Peggy to Andrew Setter, joining the Spence and Setter lines. Margaret died in 1829 at Red River Settlement. NOTE: the kidnapping tale is a cherished oral tradition, not a primary record; a variant says it was her daughter Peggy who was rescued by Andrew Setter [Verify vs primary records.]

P007.title: Andrew Setter — Orkney voyageur
P007.text: Born 1777 in Westray, Orkney; joined the HBC at York Factory in 1800 as a labourer. For 18 years he voyaged inland. In 1821 Rev. John West baptised and married him to Margaret Spence at Beaver Creek — the first HBC clergyman's marriage west of Red River. Retired to St Andrews Parish in 1823 [Verify vs primary records.]

P030.title: David Spence — MLA, Convention of Forty delegate, Métis leader
P030.text: David Spence (b. 5 Sep 1824, St. John's parish; d. 16 Sep 1885) was a Scottish Half-Breed, son of James Spence and his second wife Jane Morwick, both Métis — his mother was grandmother to Manitoba's first Premier, John Norquay. He married Catherine Hallett on 15 Feb 1844 at St. John's (daughter of Henry Hallett and Catherine Parenteau). He represented St. Anne's at the 1870 Convention of Forty, and in 1877 the family moved to lot #62 at Poplar Point. He was elected the first MLA from Poplar Point on 27 Dec 1870 and served 1870-74, also serving as Justice of the Peace for Poplar Point and Marquette. Métis scrip was issued to David and Catherine on 2 Oct 1876. Catherine died in 1880. David was accidentally shot in his own home by a neighbour who thought the rifle was unloaded, and died of the wound on 16 Sep 1885.

P022.title: Elizabeth Setter — married a Premier
P022.text: Daughter of George Setter; in 1862 married John Norquay, who in 1878 became Manitoba's first Métis Premier. Through her, this family connects to Manitoba's provincial founding [Verify vs primary records.]

P051.title: Premier John Norquay — cousin by marriage
P051.text: Manitoba's first Métis Premier (1878-87). Married Elizabeth Setter, daughter of George Setter. A towering figure in early Manitoba politics [Verify vs primary records.]

P067.title: Gerhard & Geeske De Vries — Dutch settlers
P067.text: Dutch immigrants from Friesland, Netherlands. Married 4 Oct 1929 in Ochre River MB; homesteaded on the south shore of Lake Dauphin in the Turtle River District. Raised 11 children on the farm.

P049.title: Bryon Edward deVries — HR Director, family man
P049.text: Born 17 Jul 1954; died 13 Oct 2019. Director of Human Resources at Sunrise School Division (and previously WRHA). Remembered for hosting Sunday family dinners for 20+ years, coaching soccer, and his devotion to helping anyone.

P046.title: Mavis Irene (Hamilton) Lau
P046.text: Born 1 Sep 1933 in Tisdale SK; moved to Flin Flon at 6. Only daughter of six children. A remarkable seamstress, knitter, cross-stitcher, curler, golfer and bridge player; worked at Sears in Flin Flon until retirement.

P079.title: Isaac Batt — English fur-trader, your Métis gateway
P079.text: Isaac Batt (c1725-1791) was an English Hudson's Bay Company trader born in Hertfordshire, England. He contracted with the HBC in 1754 as a labourer at York Factory (£10/yr) and rose to be an experienced inland canoeman, steersman and trader. He travelled inland under the personal guidance of leading Cree chiefs (Wapinesiw, Matonabbee) and worked alongside Samuel Hearne trying to establish Cumberland House. Illiterate, he never rose past £20/yr as literate juniors outranked him; in 1775 he briefly deserted to rival 'Pedlar' traders, returning in 1777. He had a Cree family by 1777 — his daughter Margaret 'Nestichio' Batt is the Métis root of this line. He died in summer 1791 near Manchester House, shot through the head by an Indian guide during a buffalo hunt, the first HBC servant killed by Indians in the Saskatchewan area. James Spence Sr's 1795 will left legacies to 'his Indian Wife Nestichio, daughter of the deceased Isaac Batt' and their four children, confirming the link in primary records.
